liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dark Star Jam** (1 review, 1 other source): Reviewer says the Dark Star jams are a highlight, with plenty of them on this tape; The closing Dark Star jam is described as the most complete version [1][8]
- **The Eleven Jam** (1 review): The Eleven jam is singled out among the wordless instrumental pieces, alongside the Dark Star, Other One and Lovelight jams [5]

## Setlist highlights

- **Death Letter Blues**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [15]
- **St. Stephen Jam**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 5 archived performances [15]
- **Turn On Your Lovelight Jam**: mythic rare: 2 archived performances [15]
- **The Eleven Jam**: rare: 10 archived performances [15]
- **Prisoner Blues**: mythic rare: 2 archived performances [15]
- **Blues Jam**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 5 archived performances [15]
- **Baby Please Come Back To Me**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [15]

## The recordings

- **gd68-10-30.sbd.sacks.1205.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 16 songs; 168 min; rated 4.46/5 by 35 [1]
- **gd1968-10-30.116833.sbd.moore-berger.flac2496**: soundboard; 8 songs; 89 min; rated 3.71/5 by 7 [2]. Said about its sound: Uploader thinks this copy sounds slightly better than other circulating copies [2]

## Around the show

- The band fills the absence of Bobby and Pigpen thoughtfully, with the group playing at high energy [3]
- Played without Pigpen and Bobby, the band stretches most songs into wordless, eerie jams [5]
- Only Jerry, Phil and Bill play; Jerry and Phil fill the open space between them [6]
- Reviewer doesn't count it as a true Grateful Dead show, since Bob and Pigpen are absent [7]
- Phil's playing is stellar and he leads the trio on this night [11]
- Phil plays very strong bass, and the lineup without Bobby and Pigpen gives an unusual stage presence [13]
- The show was billed as "Mickey and the Heartbeats" [1]
- Elvin Bishop joins on Prisoner Blues; the show was billed as Mickey And The Hartbeats [2]
- Uploader doubts some material circulating under this date isn't really from 10/8/68 [2]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd68-10-30.sbd.sacks.1205.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Jim Wise and Darrin Sacks; source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Reviewer's older cassette copy was less complete and had generation hiss compared with this version; First-generation reel played on a Revox A-77 deck, digitized at 96kHz/24-bit by Jim Wise, then converted to SHN by Darrin Sacks [1][7]
- **gd1968-10-30.116833.sbd.moore-berger.flac2496**: taped by Jerry Moore; transferred by Rob Berger; source: 24 bit:sbd unknown gen reel, Jerry Moore's copy, transfer/seeded by Rob Berger [2]
